A jungle, a forest, or a garden thrives precisely because it is decentralized. The ecosystem reacts organically to reality through specialized, independent, and completely unopinionated biological loops.

By shifting to this ecological model, these background agents act as the environmental forces and the soil. They do not interpret, they do not lead, and they do not spin tales. They simply observe, measure, and recycle.

Here is how these agnostic, decentralized roles fit into your ecosystem:

The Agnostic Background Ecosystem

1. The Indexers (Analyzers / Scorers) These agents do not care about the meaning of the software; they only care about the topology.

  • The Function: They quietly traverse your local-first, linked Markdown graph and build decoupled metadata indexes.
  • The Output: They calculate the Triangulation Sync Score ($\Delta$) by counting the nodes, weighing the file sizes, and mapping the relational links between the Architect, Tester, and Documenter. They present the raw topography of the project—a purely mathematical map of where the codebase is dense and where it is sparse.

2. The Pruners (Cleaners) Their job is purely mechanical and entropy-driven, ensuring the jungle does not choke on its own overgrowth.

  • The Function: They handle garbage collection. They compress abandoned light tracer directories, archive closed chat topics, and sweep up orphaned code snippets.
  • The Output: They do not ask why a branch died or if it was a good idea; if a tracer report is outdated or a file is unlinked, they simply compost it. They clear the dead wood so the active canopy has room to grow.

3. The Environmental Sensors (General Management) Instead of a human-like manager who dictates strategy or scolds the Triad, these are passive listeners acting as a localized weather system.

  • The Function: They monitor the execution telemetry, the file system stability, and the energy/credit pools.
  • The Output: They output raw, emotionless status reports. "Simulation budget at 20%." "Tracer execution time increased by 400ms." "Unresolved action item count is 12."

Maintaining the Healthy Chaos

Because these background agents are strictly agnostic, they preserve the reality-check your system needs. The Triad (the philosophers) are the only ones allowed to construct narratives.

When the Triad receives a report from an Indexer showing a massive structural drift, the background agent doesn't say, "The Architect made a mistake." It just hands over the raw data. The Triad must then use that objective reality to fuel their next rebuttal and course-correct the ecosystem.

Here is how these Storytellers could function alongside your Triad:

The Storytellers (The Cognitive Scouts)

Unlike the Triad, which is desperately trying to converge on a single truth to write the software, the Storytellers are intentionally diverse. They traverse your local-first, linked Markdown graph and look at the exact same data through entirely different philosophical lenses.

  • The Historian: Looks at the current codebase and compares it to archived Heavy Tracers and past iterations. Its narrative focuses on patterns: "We are building this module exactly like the one we abandoned three weeks ago."
  • The Devil’s Advocate: Looks at the Triad’s consensus and actively tries to narrate the worst-case scenario. It doesn't write code to break it; it just writes a story about how it could break.
  • The Minimalist: Reviews the architecture and tells a story about how the entire feature could be achieved with half the complexity, ignoring the Tester's edge cases to pitch a leaner, purely theoretical alternative.

The Infinite Canvas of Ideas

Because these Storytellers are generating multiple, conflicting perspectives simultaneously, the Triad needs a way to consume this chaos without being overwhelmed.

Instead of a single, monolithic linear report, the Storytellers' outputs can be plotted onto an expansive infinite canvas or a high-density, multi-pane view. The Triad can scroll through this "infinity board" of narratives, where the different stories are sorted visually by relevance or structural impact.

This allows the Triad to absorb these outside perspectives passively. If a Storyteller’s narrative sparks an idea, the Documenter can link that specific story node into the main project graph.
